chunks: Indeed, those who believe, and the Jews and the Sabians and the Christians, whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does good, will have no fear nor will they grieve.
ai.seo_question: Who are the groups mentioned in this verse and what is the condition for their salvation?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted through the lens of 'al-walā’ wa al-barā’', where the specific groups (Jews, Sabians, Christians) are viewed as representatives of broader categories of monotheists who maintained fidelity to their original prophets. The condition of 'working righteousness' is understood not merely as ritual observance but as adherence to the core tenets of Tawhid and the Prophethood of Muhammad (PBUH) as recognized by each community. This highlights a universalist criterion for salvation based on sincere belief and action, while maintaining the distinct theological position of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the ultimate authority of divine guidance.
